title: ALP SoC Specification v1
description: Machine-readable per-SoC specification consumed by alp-sdk tooling and downstream consumers (alp-studio, etc.). The SDK's per-SoM preset `silicon:` ref (e.g. "alif:ensemble:e3") resolves into one of these files under metadata/socs/<vendor>/<family>/<part>.json.

soc_spec_version.description: Schema version. Bumped on breaking changes.

ref.description: Canonical reference like "alif:ensemble:e3" — used by the SDK loader + downstream consumers to look this file up.

pending_alif_datasheet.description: When true, this file was populated from secondary sources (ALP module datasheet, family pattern). Replace with primary datasheet data before locking metadata for production.

pending_reference_manual_ingestion.description: When true, the per-peripheral counts and any other Reference-Manual-derived fields have not yet been extracted (RM ingestion still pending). peripherals: {} on such a SoC means "unknown / TBD", not "silicon has no peripherals". Downstream tooling MUST treat ALP_SOC_*_COUNT ceilings as under-reporting until this flag is cleared.

_pending_reason.description: Optional sibling rationale for pending_reference_manual_ingestion / pending_alif_datasheet. Free-form note describing what is pending and why, since JSON itself has no native comment syntax.

source.description: Filename of the PDF the data was extracted from.

hwrm.description: Optional pointer to a Hardware Reference Manual that supplements the datasheet (Alif Ensemble family uses these heavily). The PDF itself does not live in the repo; this block carries provenance only.

source.description: Filename of the PDF the data was extracted from.

confidential.description: When true, the PDF is NDA-bound and stays out of git. The block is kept here for traceability.

errata.description: Optional vendor errata documents the SoC is subject to. Per-item ids + workarounds let the metadata pipeline surface affected silicon revisions to the studio.

title_quirk.description: Notes about discrepancies between the PDF title and its actual scope.

soc_ram_kb.description: Maximum on-die SRAM in KB across all variants. Per-variant overrides go into variants[].sram_kb.

inference_arena_sram_kib.description: Usable SRAM budget (KiB) for an NPU tensor arena on this SoC. The .alpmodel loader admits a blob only if its requires.sram_kib <= this budget. 0 = unknown/unbounded (fit-check skips, and alp_model_select_result_t::arena_fit_unverified is set on the winning selection so the skip is not silent -- see src/backends/inference/alp_model_select.h). This is NOT a datasheet constant: it is an integration/partition decision (how much on-die SRAM this SKU's firmware reserves for the NPU tensor arena vs. everything else), which is why every real SoC in this repo carries 0 today (issue #1731) -- author per-SoC only when that partition decision is actually made, never a plausible-looking guess.

tcm_kb.description: Maximum tightly-coupled memory in KB (informative; per-core TCM lives in cores[].tcm_kb).

soc_flash_mb.description: Maximum on-die non-volatile memory in MB (MRAM on Alif). Per-variant overrides go into variants[].mram_mb.

always_on_sram_kb.description: Always-on / utility SRAM that survives STOP mode.

zephyr_peripherals_dtsi.description: OPTIONAL `#include <...>` path of the alp-sdk devicetree overlay declaring THIS SoC's peripheral and NPU node set (e.g. "alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi", which lives at zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi). `scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py --emit zephyr-board` emits it verbatim into the generated board .dts. Declared per SoC rather than derived from `part` because a wrong overlay produces a board that builds and then misbehaves on silicon -- the E8's overlay declares `ethosu85`, while an E3 carries 2x Ethos-U55 and no U85 -- so a SoC with no overlay of its own must REFUSE to generate a board rather than inherit a sibling part's. Omit for SoCs the board generator does not fully cover.

peripherals.description: Counts per peripheral kind. Studio uses these to validate which blocks fit on the SoC. Use the SAME keys across vendors so the studio can do generic matching.

peripherals_unverified.description: Subset of THIS file's `peripherals` keys whose count has no datasheet/DFP/HWRM/SVD citation (inherited from a sibling, carried forward from an early ingestion pass, or otherwise asserted without a primary source). Distinct from `pending_reference_manual_ingestion`, which marks the WHOLE block unaudited on an otherwise-placeholder file; this field flags specific gaps on a file that IS mostly grounded (issue #936). `gen_soc_caps.py` surfaces the listed keys as a comment above the SoC's block in soc_caps.h; `validate_metadata.py` warns (non-fatal) if a listed key isn't actually present in `peripherals`.

peripheral_instances.description: OPTIONAL sibling to `peripherals`, keyed by a SUBSET of `peripherals`' keys (issue #1154). `peripherals` stays the count map every existing consumer (gen_soc_caps.py, gen_support_matrix.py, validate_metadata.py, the studio compat pass) reads; this block adds, per key that has a grounded 1:1 source, one entry per physical instance with its register base/size and interrupt lines, mechanically projected from a vendored Zephyr SoC devicetree (see scripts/gen_soc_peripheral_instances.py's module docstring for the exact source + the documented coverage gaps). A key absent here is NOT a claim the class doesn't exist -- it means no grounded per-instance source has been projected yet, exactly like an absent `peripherals` key means unknown, not zero. Never hand-edit; regenerate.

index.description: Instance/channel number, taken from the devicetree node's own `channel` cell (never inferred from array position).

compatible.description: Devicetree `compatible` string the instance was matched on, e.g. "renesas,rz-riic".

base.description: Register window base address, lowercase 0x-prefixed hex (matching the devicetree's own `i2c@44400400` literal style), from the devicetree node's `reg` property. A decimal or uppercase-hex value fails this pattern rather than being silently accepted -- see issue #1154's PR review.

size.description: Register window size in bytes, lowercase 0x-prefixed hex, from the same `reg` property.

interrupts.description: One entry per devicetree `interrupts` cell pair, in source order.

name.description: From the paired `interrupt-names` cell, when present.

capabilities.description: Silicon-determined feature flags. SoM YAMLs may override or extend specific keys via their own capabilities: block (e.g., V2N declares cau: true because the on-module GD32 bridge provides CAU even though the host silicon does not).

inline_aes.description: Inline AES extension on the host core.

packages.description: All packages in which this SoC is offered, regardless of variant. Per-variant package selection lives in variants[].package.

variants.description: Orderable SKUs. Each entry corresponds to one row of the datasheet's Ordering Information table. alp-studio presents these as user-selectable choices when the SKU is configurable.

memory_regions.description: SoC-level fixed memory regions with base addresses.  Used by _resolve_memory_map when the SoM preset has no explicit memory_map: block and the variant sram_banks_kb does not carry base addresses (e.g. Renesas RZ/V2N OCRAM + DDR window).  Entries follow the som-preset memory_map: shape.

notes.description: Freeform extraction notes worth preserving (caveats, page references, ambiguities).

access_windows.description: OPTIONAL per-core addressable sub-window of the region, keyed by core id.  `accessible_from:` is a yes/no per core and cannot express "this core reaches only PART of the region" -- the RZ/V2N Cortex-M33 does exactly that (FSP bsp_slave_address.h: CM33-secure 0x80000000 / CM33-non-secure 0x90000000 -> A55 0x40000000, 256 MiB) while ddr_main spans 4 GiB.  Declare the reachable slice here and scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py confines that core's IPC carve-outs to it instead of allocating at the region top, where the address does not exist for that core.  Omit for regions every accessible_from core reaches in full.

base.description: Window base in the SAME address space as the region's own `base` (i.e. the physical/host view), NOT the aliased address the core issues.

note.description: Provenance for the window -- name the vendor header/manual it was read from.

id.description: Canonical core identifier used by board.yaml cores: and SoM preset topology: blocks. Unique within a SoC.

zephyr_cpucluster.description: Zephyr multi-image board qualifier for this core (e.g. "rtss_hp", "cm33") -- the `<board>/<soc>/<cpucluster>` third segment `scripts/alp_project.py --emit zephyr-board` uses to name per-core board artefacts. Distinct from `id` because upstream Zephyr's own cluster-naming convention doesn't always match the SDK's core id.

itcm_global_base.description: System-bus-visible alias base address (decimal) of this core's ITCM window, when the vendor fork's devicetree exposes one (e.g. Alif Ensemble RTSS cores). Consumed by `--emit zephyr-board` to retarget the `&itcm` node's `global_base` property; omit for cores with no such alias.

dtcm_global_base.description: System-bus-visible alias base address (decimal) of this core's DTCM window. See itcm_global_base.

paired_core.description: `cores[].id` of the CPU core this NPU instance is wired to (Alif: the High-Efficiency M55 drives the 128-MAC high-efficiency Ethos-U55, the High-Performance M55 the 256-MAC high-perf one). Lets the build emit size the accelerator per target core instead of assuming the SoC's most-capable instance. Omit for a shared / non-core-paired NPU (e.g. the E8 U85 on the HG subsystem).

mac_per_cycle.description: Required for every ethos-u* NPU -- the emit's accelerator sizing (scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig.py) and target derivation (scripts/alp_model/targets.py) both read npus[].mac_per_cycle directly for this backend; an absent value either raises KeyError (targets.py) or falls through to a silent 256-MAC default (kconfig.py) instead of failing at the metadata source (#1849).

gops.description: Giga ops per second.  Provide either gops or tops (= gops × 1000).

tops.description: Tera ops per second.  Provide either gops or tops.

external.description: true when the accelerator is a separate IC (e.g. DEEPX DX-M1).

order_code.description: Vendor part number. For Alif Ensemble this is the 16-character base PN (without -T / -Y shipment suffix).

part_number_root.description: Vendor short name without the package / temperature / qualification suffix (e.g. "i.MX 9352"). Provided when the full order code is awaiting the maintainer's HW-config writeup.

notes.description: Per-variant freeform notes (provenance, pending fields, etc.).

package.description: Package identifier, e.g. WLCSP208, FBGA194. Optional when only the short part-number root is known; promoted to required for production variants once the HW-config writeup lands.

temperature_grade.description: Vendor temperature grade. Maps loosely to operating_temp_c; the canonical numeric range still lives at the SoC level.

sram_banks_kb.description: Per-bank SRAM sizes in KB. Studio uses this for memory-map planning. Bank labels match datasheet (SRAM0, SRAM2 (M55-HP ITCM), etc.).

optional_features.description: Per-variant on/off feature toggles. Common keys: npu_hp, npu_hg, can_fd, isp, jpeg_encoder.

shipment_suffixes.description: Shipment packaging suffixes appended to order_code, e.g. ["-T" (Tape and Reel), "-Y" (Tray)].

alp_module_skus.description: Alp Lab module SKUs (e.g. E1M-AEN801) that ship this Alif variant. Lets the studio resolve E1M SKU → SoC variant in one hop.

zephyr_soc_variant.description: Zephyr upstream SOC_* Kconfig / devicetree symbol this variant builds against, when it differs from `order_code` (e.g. a die upstream Zephyr doesn't model separately because it's devicetree-identical to a sibling it does model). `--emit zephyr-board` uses this in place of order_code for board filenames / Kconfig selects when present.

debug.description: Debug-probe identity for this variant (#987), consumed by alp-sdk-vscode to generate a working cortex-debug launch.json without human input. Every key is optional -- an absent key is a published 'unknown', not a guess, and must be copied verbatim from the owning tool's own list or a working in-tree invocation; a plausible-looking guess fails at the probe rather than at validation. EXCEPTION: `jlink_flash_device` on an Alif Ensemble SoC is not optional -- see its own description below and scripts/validate_metadata.py::_check_soc_jlink_flash_device_declared.

pyocd_target.description: pyOCD target id (cortex-debug `targetId` for servertype `pyocd`). For Alif Ensemble parts this is the variant's own `order_code` -- confirmed 1:1 against the CMSIS-Pack index (pack AlifSemiconductor.Ensemble 2.2.0, released 2026-06-30, github.com/alifsemi/alif_ensemble-cmsis-dfp tag v2.2.0). Note: the DFP checkout used elsewhere in this repo for order-code/core spelling is pinned at v2.1.0 (2025-12-19) -- 2.1.0 is simply older than this citation, not a mismatch; the order-code spelling itself is unchanged between the two (both list AE822FA0E5597BS0 / LS0 identically).

jlink_device.description: SEGGER J-Link **attach/debug** device name (cortex-debug `device` for servertype `jlink`) for a live core, keyed by `cores[].id`. On Alif Ensemble this is the GENERIC `Cortex-M55` for every M55 core, not a part-number profile: `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:108-119` documents two distinct J-Link identities. On a J-Link DLL older than V9.46 the part-number profile 'will NOT connect to a live/running secure core' -- corroborated by `docs/_aen-runbook-section.md:255` (`Could not connect to the target device` when the part profile is used to attach on an old DLL) -- but on V9.46+ the part-number profile also connects to a live core (`docs/aen-bench-bringup.md:14`, bench-confirmed 2026-06-16); the generic profile remains the documented choice for read/RAM-run regardless of DLL version, and is what was originally bench-proven to attach (CPUID `0x411FD220` / SW-DP IDR `0x4C013477`). The part-number profile is a *separate* fact -- see `jlink_flash_device`. Validated against cores[].id by scripts/validate_metadata.py::_check_soc_debug_probe_identity.

jlink_flash_device.description: SEGGER J-Link **part-number device profile**, used ONLY to unlock J-Link's built-in Flow D MRAM loader (`scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:108-114`) -- on a J-Link DLL older than V9.46 it cannot attach to a live/running core (use `jlink_device` for that); on V9.46+ it also attaches, but `jlink_device`'s generic profile stays the documented choice for read/RAM-run regardless. It is not per-core: both `scripts/bench/aen/flash-jlink-hp.sh` and `flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` select the SAME device string regardless of which core they flash, so this is a single per-variant string, not a jlink_device-shaped map. Populate only from a canonical entry in the vendor's own device database (e.g. SEGGER J-Link DLL `JLINKARM_DEVICE_GetInfo` readback) -- never derive it from a naming convention, and never publish an order-code alias that merely happens to resolve. `null` is a DECLARED known-unknown: this variant's device profile is genuinely unresolved (e.g. an order code the vendor device DB does not carry under any spelling) -- consumers must refuse rather than silently choose another transport. tan's `flow_d_available()` tests key PRESENCE, so a present-but-null value deliberately reaches `plan_alif_mram_jlink` and becomes the loud refusal it already produces for every other malformed Flow D field, instead of a silent Flow-A (SE-UART) fallback. ABSENCE of this key is NOT a permitted way to spell 'unknown' on an Alif Ensemble SoC: a missing key is exactly what silently downgrades Flow D to Flow A with no diagnostic (#1295) -- every Alif Ensemble variant must publish either the string or explicit null, enforced by scripts/validate_metadata.py::_check_soc_jlink_flash_device_declared.

expect_dpidr.description: The ADIv5 SW-DP IDR (DPIDR) this variant's debug port answers, as a 32-bit `0x`-prefixed hex constant -- the wrong-board guard a host flasher reads BEFORE any write, while the session is still read-only (#1355). This is a property of the DEBUG PORT, not of a core: it is one per-variant string, not a `jlink_device`-shaped per-core map. Populate ONLY from a measurement on real silicon (`Found SW-DP with ID <id>` in a J-Link/pyOCD connect log) -- an absent key is the correct published 'unknown' and simply leaves the guard unarmed, whereas a GUESSED value is strictly worse than absent: if it happens to match some other board on the same bench it makes the guard pass on exactly the board it exists to exclude. Consumed as `flash_args.expect_dpidr`, and PAIRED there with this variant's per-core `jlink_device` (the live-core read attach profile) -- a downstream consumer refuses a half-armed pair, so a variant publishing `expect_dpidr` must also publish `jlink_device` for every core (enforced by scripts/validate_metadata.py::_check_soc_debug_probe_identity).

openocd_config.description: OpenOCD board/target config file path relative to OpenOCD's own scripts/ tree (cortex-debug `configFiles[]` for servertype `openocd`). No SoC family in this repo has one today (verified absent from OpenOCD upstream master's tcl/target + tcl/board for Alif Ensemble and Renesas RZ/V2N as of this issue) -- schema-only until a vendor config exists; do not populate with a guess.

svd.description: CMSIS-SVD register description for a live core (cortex-debug `svdFile`), keyed by `cores[].id` exactly as the sibling `jlink_device` is, each value a BARE RELATIVE PATH -- never absolute, never containing `..`, never a URL (#948; shape enforced by scripts/validate_metadata.py::_check_soc_debug_svd_shape, which also validates every key against cores[].id). KEYED BY CORE, NOT PER VARIANT: an SVD is one core's register view of the SoC, not the part's. The Alif DFP ships `<order_code>_CM55_HE_View.svd` and `<order_code>_CM55_HP_View.svd` as separate files, and `scripts/gen_rzv2n_cm33_svd.py` emits a CM33-only view for a SoC that also has A55s. `expect_dpidr` and `jlink_flash_device` are per-variant and each argues why in its own description; this key cannot make that argument, so it takes the shape the data has. A map is also what stops the specific mistake called out below -- with one string per variant, attaching an HE register map to an HP session is not a mistake a consumer could avoid. Sparse is fine: declare only the cores whose view you actually have (the A-class core typically has none). RESOLUTION ORDER, in this order: the repository directory first, then the `ALP_SVD_DIR` environment variable -- modelled on the `SETOOLS_DIR` pattern this repo already uses for genuinely licence-gated vendor tooling. ABSENCE SEMANTICS: an unresolvable path is NOT an error -- the consumer omits `svdFile` from the launch config and the session runs without a Cortex Peripherals view, which costs a register pane and nothing else. Never substitute another variant's SVD: a register map from the wrong part is worse than none, because it reads plausibly. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY DECLARES THIS KEY YET, deliberately -- whether Alp Lab redistributes a vendor's SVD under that vendor's own terms is a per-vendor maintainer decision (ADR 0032 records the mechanism, not an authorisation), so the only supported source today is a customer-supplied file reached through `ALP_SVD_DIR`. If vendored SVDs ever land they go in the segregated subtree ADR 0032 describes, with the vendor's unmodified licence file beside them, and the existence half of the gate begins applying to them.
